packages.headline: Quarantine Zone’s Miami Zero DLC is the Perfect Excuse to Return to the Smash Hit Zombie Checkpoint Simulator

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
Learn why the free Miami Zero DLC makes it the best time ever to jump into Quarantine Zone, available on Game Pass.
Quarantine Zone’s Miami Zero DLC is the Perfect Excuse to Return to the Smash Hit Zombie Checkpoint Simulator
Earlier this year, zombie checkpoint simulator Quarantine Zone took the world by storm. Millions of you stepped up to protect this undead-ravaged outpost at the end of the world, screening survivors, weeding out the infected, and uncovering the mystery of the outbreak. But it’s been a while, right? You’ve probably moved on, hung up your scanner, and forgotten all about Georgie and all the other brave souls protecting the last remnants of humanity. But it’s time to go back. Way back.
Miami Zero is a massive free expansion that transports you to the sun-soaked (and frequently rain-soaked) streets of Miami, back to when the virus was first unleashed on the world. This was ground zero for the outbreak and in this DLC you’ll find yourself right in the thick of it, screening desperate survivors, identifying symptoms, and making tough calls about who lives and who dies. The fate of the world rests on your shoulders, and your scanner, but hey – at least the sun is shining!
So far, so familiar. But Miami Zero is much more than just a change of scenery. This is a major update to the game, adding new inspection mechanics, tools, survivors, minigames, quests, and more. We’ve been releasing regular updates for Quarantine Zone since it launched in January, but this is by far the biggest chunk of new stuff yet. We’ve also taken the opportunity to let your imaginations run wild, and some of the new content we’ve been cooking up is a little wild ‘n’ wacky, just like Miami itself.
If you’ve played Quarantine Zone you’ll know that you spend a lot of time getting familiar (maybe too familiar) with the people lining up for processing. In the Miami Zero expansion, the flavour and variety of these characters has been dramatically increased. Over 30 unique survivors have been added to the game, all with their own distinct personalities, voice lines, appearances, and quirks. We’ve also added new animations, additional body type variety, and lots of new reactions to really make the game’s characters come to life. You never know who’ll show up next.
New survivors also means new symptoms. Whether it’s suspicious scars, rotten organs, or wriggly stomach parasites, there are lots of wonderfully disgusting new things to discover as you use your various high-tech screening tools to probe the potentially infected. But, this being the city of vice, it’s not just signs of infection you have to search for – there are drugs to sniff out too. This illicit contraband can be slipped under hats, swallowed, hidden in a fist, or concealed in other tricky ways, adding a whole extra layer of inspection gameplay to the classic Quarantine Zone experience.
Miami Zero also introduces a new research centre that lets you perform experiments on the infected – with surprising and shocking results, including freakish mutants that could threaten the safety of the checkpoint. Or if you’d rather escape, why not try your hand at a campaign-spanning quest to repair a ship and sail to calmer waters. This combined with a new campaign, storyline, quests, and characters means Miami Zero is absolutely stuffed with new content. Oh, and you can feed people to sharks. Did we mention that? You just better make doubly sure they’re infected first.
For the authentic Miami experience, we’ve also added a new dynamic weather system to the game. From cloud-splitting sunshine to dust storms and tropical rain, the elements are as unpredictable as the people who’ll come through the checkpoint. We’ve also added new locations and scenery, including a pier, city streets, and a music festival, as well as upgrades to the game’s environmental audio. packages.headline: Peak climbs its way onto PS5 October 22

sources.label: PlayStation Blog
sources.evidenceText:
Ascend with friends using crossplay co-op.
Peak climbs its way onto PS5 October 22
Hello Scouts! Team Peak is happy to announce that our climbing game Peak is launching on PlayStation 5 October 22. Peak is a collaboration between two studios, Aggro Crab and Landfall, together, we make Team Peak.
The result was Peak, a co-op climbing game where the slightest mistake can spell your doom. You play solo or as a group of lost nature scouts, with your only hope of rescue from a mysterious island being to scale the mountain at its centre.
The key is to stick together, help each other out, and to find the best way to the top before hunger, hazards, or the fog gets you.
After the game jam the team went home to their respective countries, with Landfall finishing up our game Haste, and Aggro Crab working on Peak and some other projects. We then all met back up in Sweden in June to finish the game together – and to celebrate the Swedish tradition of Midsummer.
Peak is a game based on friendship, both in its development and gameplay.
In the game, there’s an important rule: Never abandon a friend in need. Therefore, we’re excited that with the launch on PS5 we’ve also made it possible for crossplay so that you can climb with up to three friends no matter what platform they use.
The Mountain Takes no Prisoners! Climb through 4 biomes on your way to the Peak, each with its own life-threatening obstacles. You’ll need to scavenge for questionable food to survive and manage your injuries carefully – every setback limits your stamina, making it harder to climb.
Aggro Crab is an American studio based in Seattle, Washington, known for their games Another Crab’s Treasure and Going Under. Landfall is a Swedish studio based in Stockholm, known for games like Content Warning, Haste, Totally Accurate Battle Simulator, Stick Fight: The Game, and many more.
Both studios became friends after meeting at a game developer conference in 2022, instantly kicking it off. After the success of Another Crab’s Treasure and Content Warning, the teams thought that it could be cool to collaborate on a small project together.

sources.evidenceText:
Gaming Factoryは10月15日、オープンワールド・レースゲーム『JDM: Ph4ntom Driver』を発表した。
「群魂県」オープンワールドレース『JDM: Ph4ntom Driver』発表。なぜか異界化した群玉県、妖怪たちを轢きまくる殺意高め走り屋ゲーム
デベロッパーのGaming Factoryは10月15日、オープンワールド・レースゲーム『 JDM: Ph4ntom Driver 』を発表した。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam）で、配信時期は未定。
本作は、オープンワールド・レースゲーム『JDM: Japanese Drift Master』のスピンオフ作品だ。アクション性を重視したアーケードスタイルのゲームプレイが採用され、妖怪などの怪異が登場する。
『JDM: Ph4ntom Driver』の舞台となるのは、前作『JDM: Japanese Drift Master』に登場した架空の日本の県である「群玉県」の異界バージョン「群魂県」だ。現世から隔絶された群魂県は、邪悪な魔力に侵され、さまざまな妖怪が生息。プレイヤーはこの世界で生き延びながら、魔王である瘴呑童子との決戦に挑むことになる。
本作では、JDMマシンを運転してオープンワールドの群魂県を探索する。街では、敵である妖怪が群れをなして襲ってきて、マシンで薙ぎ倒していくようなゲームプレイとなるようだ。また、探索する中では新たなマシンやパーツを入手でき、愛車をカスタマイズし性能と戦闘能力を強化していくことができる。
シングルプレイのキャンペーンモードでは、前作『JDM: Japanese Drift Master』と同じく漫画風のカットシーンと、会話システムを通じて物語が展開されていく。「ボリュームたっぷり」とのことである。また、マルチプレイモードの実装も予定されており、こちらの情報は今後発表される。
本作は、もともとは『JDM: Japanese Drift Master』向けの拡張パックとして計画されていたが、開発を進める中で、ゲームの基本的な仕組みを大幅に変更したいと考えるようになり、スピンオフさせた経緯があるとのこと。その後、本作は野心的なプロジェクトへと発展し、規模もますます大きくなっていったという。なお、前作未プレイでも楽しめるが、ファンであれば気づくようなイースターエッグやオマージュが仕込まれているそうだ。

packages.headline: 33 New Details From the GTA 6 Launch Trailer

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
GTA 6's launch trailer may only be 90 seconds long, but there's plenty to see - here's the 33 details we spotted.
33 New Details From the GTA 6 Launch Trailer
Did you spot the GTA 1 reference?
Yet another look at GTA 6 has come our way, which means it’s time to get forensic; we’ve gone through the new trailer with a fine-tooth comb to pick out all of the interesting details hidden within. From peeks at what’s in store for some of its most explosive missions, further insights into Jason’s military past, and more than one visit to a steamy shower, there’s plenty of new things to take a look at.
Let’s not waste any more time. Here are the 33 details we spotted in the GTA 6 launch trailer.
Multiple shots offer a closer look at Jason and paint a pretty clear picture of the kind of man we’ll be taking control of. We already knew that he was ex-military, but midway through the trailer we see him wearing a U.S. Army T-shirt that offers more details on his service.
1. Firstly, the combat training school Jason seemingly trained at is located in North Fort Law. Longtime fans will recognise this as the military base from the very first Grand Theft Auto game. In that original game, it was located in the state of New Guernsey, but it’s more likely that the one Jason attended is in the State of Alderney, the HD universe’s take on New Jersey. We know that Lucia is from Liberty City, which is located in the neighboring State of Liberty – perhaps they met when Jason was stationed at the base?
2. More prominent than that small print is the word “Marauder,” which matches the skull-and-parachute tattoo on Jason’s arm that we’ve seen in previous videos. The Marauders are presumably the unit he served in, and may be a reference to the real-life Merrill's Marauders, a 1940s special forces group. Its modern-day equivalent is the 75th Ranger Regiment, and so it’s likely that Jason was a ranger.
3. It seems like Jason has fallen on tough times since he left the forces. “I got in some trouble in the army, didn’t leave on the best of terms,” he says in the trailer’s opening. “They don’t give loans, anything, to people like me.” With a situation like that, it’s no wonder Jason has resorted to crime. The cost of living is only going up!

Maestro Media recently announced a new board game adaptation of the popular mobile game Clash Royale . Now, IGN can exclusively reveal that Maestro Media will be launching a Kickstarter campaign in support of the final product: Clash Royale: The Grand Arena this month
The Kickstarter, which is aiming to launch on October 20, follows the successful crowdfunding of Maestro’s previous collaboration with Supercell, Clash of Clans: The Epic Raid . Ahead of the campaign, we got the chance to speak with the board game’s lead designer, David Gordon, about how the team approached bringing the mobile hit to the tabletop.
First, we learned a little more about what to expect from the board game itself, which you can get the gist of in this exclusive trailer:
The Grand Arena generally adapts the deck-building and strategy elements of the mobile app into a board game. Yep, that means fans will finally be able to build Clash Royale decks with real cardboard.
The tabletop game is designed for two to four players. Each player controls their own forces, which consist of eight-card decks built around a chosen Champion. Cards will be based on the mobile game’s card list, plenty of which feature characters and items going back to the original Clash of Clans era.
In-game, players take turns to try and destroy other players’ Towers while also protecting their own. The board features two lanes, and players must determine where exactly to play cards to launch attacks, plant defensive units, and use items. Players can’t endlessly cycle through their cards, either, as moves are limited by the classic Clash resource, Elixir.
Destroying another player’s Tower nets you a Crown, and the player with the most Crowns at the end wins.

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Diablo 5 is still a few years away, but it looks like development is trucking along, now that Blizzard has started filming for its cinematics.
Diablo 5 Inches Closer to Launch as Cinematics Work Begins
Diablo 5 is still a few years away , but it looks like development is trucking along, now that Blizzard has started filming for its cinematics.
Blizzard cinematic director Neil David Carter posted a photo of the motion capture stage on X / Twitter , simply saying "First shoot #Diablo5." If the cinematic team is just starting motion capture, Diablo 5 probably isn't super late in its development. However, if the cinematic team is shooting motion capture for cutscenes, then the story is mostly fleshed out already.
Luckily, in an interview with Windows Central, senior producer Tiffany Watt confirmed that Diablo 5 would be using its own fork of the Diablo 4 engine, so at least the team didn't have to start building the game from scratch. But in a game like Diablo 5, a lot of work has to go into balance, itemization and world design, and the new game is likely going to be a bit more complicated than Diablo 4 thanks to the procedurally generated maps.
First shoot #Diablo5 https://t.co/3SDU51n3ch
That's why some folks, like former co-founder of Path of Exile developer Grinding Gear Games , are skeptical that Diablo 5 is going to hit its targeted release date. After all, if Diablo 5 does launch in spring 2029, it will come out just shy of six years after Diablo 4. There was an 11-year gap between Diablo 3 and Diablo 4. The gap between Diablo 4 and Diablo 5, if all goes according to plan, will be about half as long. It's little wonder, then, that Blizzard has had to work hard to convince its players that it's not abandoning Diablo 4 early, and that the game will still get content even after Diablo 5 launches .
Only time will be able to tell whether or not Diablo 4 will continue to get updates, or will just get a handful of seasons on repeat like Diablo 3 after Diablo 4 launched. But, really, all we can do is wait and see how everything plays out. For what it's worth, Diablo 5 is shaping up to be a totally different ARPG than its predecessor, and I can't wait to see how the cinematics they're shooting now are going to turn out.
Diablo 5 will tell 'three stories,' including the past, the present desolation of Diablo's takeover, and the future 'terror forming' of Sanctuary. Diablo 5 is set roughly one century after Diablo 4, in a post-apocalyptic timeline where the Lord of Terror himself has already won and rules over a fallen Sanctuary.

Creative director Mod Ryan announced that RuneScape Reignited, a new game mode designed for both old and seasoned players to start fresh, has been canceled less than two weeks after it was first announced.
RuneScape Reignited Canceled Less Than Two Weeks After Being Announced
The news was published on October 15 in the form of an official YouTube video and blog post, where Mod Ryan revealed that Jagex’s choice to cancel Reignited was in direct response to player feedback.
“We received a ton of different perspectives from all of you, and we truly appreciate everyone sharing their views. It is super important to us because the last time we didn't listen to player feedback, combat changed forever. And it has taken us over a decade to recover from that. Now I said on stage that we would not repeat the same mistakes of the past, and I truly stand by that. Considering this, we have made the decision to cancel Reignited,” the post reads.
“It is clear that we missed the mark on this, and so we are not moving forward with it. Our goal is to see RuneScape grow again, with returning players coming back and new players joining, but never at the expense of our existing community.”
That being said, that doesn’t mean RuneScape is now without any exciting developments for new players who are looking to finally try it out for themselves; starting December 2, RuneScape will hold a 10-day free trial that will let new characters — or any character that, by that date, hasn’t been in membership since June 2 — access RuneScape Members worlds and content until December 12.
“...the future of RuneScape is still extremely bright. RuneScape will always be built for and defined by its community. So please keep letting us know when you feel we're getting it wrong and shout with that same energy when you think we're getting it right too,” he continued.
RuneCcape Reignited was revealed on October 3 during RuneFest 2026 . Essentially, it’s like WoW Forever , allowing both new and returning players to start off with a clean slate and experience the game as if everyone were playing it for the first time. However, a vocal portion of the game’s playerbase felt that this would fracture its community, arguing that it would be better for the devs to focus on ongoing updates and improvements, instead — and it seems like Jagex listened to their concerns.
"It's clear that we missed the mark on this."

そうした事情に対処するため、今回「実績セット」が新登場した。この実績セットでは、すでに存在している実績がカテゴリごとに分割され、グループ化されるようになった。たとえばアクションパズル『Portal 2』では、実績がシングルプレイ専用のものと、協力プレイのみで達成できるものの2種のカテゴリに分割されているといったかたちだ。

ちなみに開発者に向けては、本日より新たな実績エディターがリリースされている。先述の実績セットも簡単に作成できるとのことで、公式より案内がおこなわれている。興味のある開発者は こちら も参照されたい。

またDLCなどが展開されているタイトルでは、DLCや拡張パックで追加されたコンテンツに取り組むことで解除される実績も中には存在する。Valveによれば、そうした追加実績は見つけにくく、すでにゲームをクリアしたプレイヤーの達成状況が意図せず損なわれてしまうとしていた。

ブサイク武侠人生RPG『活俠傳』大型アプデで「虞小梅＆郁竹ルート」がついに実装。有志日本語化Modはほぼ同時更新の爆速対応
デベロッパーの原始鳥熊（Obb Studio）は10月15日、『 活俠傳 Legend of Mortal 』（以下、活俠傳）の大型アップデートを配信した。アップデートでは虞小梅と郁竹のシナリオルートが追加されたほか、さらなる高難度モード「勇者」が追加されるなど、ゲームシステムの調整もおこなわれている。
『活俠傳』は、13世紀初頭の中国を舞台にしたノベル主体のRPGだ。主人公の「趙活（ちょうかつ）」は武術門派「唐門」の一員である。容姿が極めて不細工な趙活は武術も弱く、雑用をこなす外弟子としてうだつの上がらない日々を過ごしている。プレイヤーはそんな趙活を育成しながら、さまざまな騒動が起きる日々を送っていく。
そんな『活俠傳』に向けて、リリース以来第二弾となる大型アップデートが配信された。同アップデートはもともと今年の9月15日に配信予定とされていたものの、複数の開発メンバーが急な体調不良に見舞われたことで、配信が一か月延期されていたものである。
今回の大型アップデートでは、ヒロインである虞小梅および郁竹に専用のシナリオルートが追加。それぞれと親しくなってイベントを進めていくことで、新たな物語を体験し、専用エンディングを迎えられるようになった。またパッチノートによると、ふたりの専用ルートのほかにもシナリオの追加・調整がおこなわれているようだ。
なお『活俠傳』の 有志制作日本語化Mod もアップデートと同日の10月15日に更新されており、今回の大型アップデートに対応したバージョンがすでに配信されている。同Modは非公式ではあるが、チームリーダーのAlpaca（羊駝）氏は公式韓国語翻訳チームのリーダーを務める人物で、日本語翻訳チームも原作者許諾のもとに活動中とされている。アップデートの公開前から翻訳作業に取り組んでいたようで、すでにModを導入すれば日本語でプレイできる状態である。
『活俠傳 Legend of Mortal』はPC（ Steam ）向けに配信中だ。 現在はセール中で10月29日まで10％オフの税込2070円で購入できる。
外弟子である趙活は掟により、唐門の武芸を直接学ぶことが禁じられている。しかし他派の技を学ぶことまでは禁止されておらず、プレイヤーは自由に趙活を鍛えていくことが可能。そして本作の物語には多彩な分岐やテキストの差分が存在し、キャラクターとの友好度や趙活の性格などによって、展開が変化していく。女性キャラクターも複数登場し、特定の女性たちには恋愛関係を深められる専用イベントルートも用意されている。マルチエンディングの物語を追い、趙活を待ち受ける運命を見届けていくのだ。

sources.label: Game Developer
sources.evidenceText:
Caves of Qud is no longer in Steam Early Access, but its upcoming DLC Diaspora will be, marking untrodden ground for the in-development program.
Caves of Qud: Diaspora breaks new ground by being the first early access DLC release on Steam
The roguelike RPG is no longer in Steam Early Access, but its upcoming DLC Diaspora will be, marking untrodden ground for the in-development program.
Caves of Qud has been in some form of development since 2007 when Freehold Games began development on it. It didn't hit Steam Early Access, the PC gaming store's program for letting in-development games be sold and shaped with community feedback, until 2015, and then spent roughly nine years doing that until a 1.0 release in 2024.
But Caves of Qud is, in a form, coming back to Early Access through its new DLC titled Diaspora , which is a first for Steam.
Generally when a game leaves the Early Access program, it's akin to a graduation. Caves of Qud bringing new content back to the model has not been done before. It is unclear if there were specific rules prohibiting this or if simply no one ever thought to do it, but DLC content usually just launches in a 1.0 state.
"I was a bit hesitant at first to be honest," Kitfox Games co-founder and head of publishing Tanya X. Short tells Game Developer. "But Jason [Grinblat] and Brian [Bucklew] were really keen to continue with the development strategy that had been so successful for the main game throughout their long Early Access."
Short points out that Valve, owner and maintainer of Steam, has been a supportive partner in these uncharted waters. Apparently the company had to make a "manual adjustment" in Steam's backend to "enable it as an option."
"Their store page review then flagged it as a bug," she added.

We spoke to the internet's favorite firearms expert, Jonathan Ferguson, about all the things games get wrong about guns and his work on Hell Let Loose: Vietnam.
‘I Can Really Nitpick Things’ – Firearms Expert Jonathan Ferguson Explains the Most Common Gun Mistakes in Games
Hell Let Loose: Vietnam has a familiar voice hiding in its loadout menu. Click on any gun or grenade and you can listen to an audio description voiced by none other than Jonathan Ferguson, Keeper of Firearms and Artillery at the Royal Armouries Museum in Leeds . Ferguson has become something of a cult figure at the intersection of firearms history and video games, thanks to his detailed breakdowns of video game weapons on YouTube, but he also now plays a part in the development of video games, thanks to the Royal Armouries' consultation service. He’s worked with studios such as Team17, Facepunch, and Rebellion to ensure their weapons are as accurate as possible and avoid commonly-made mistakes, such as getting shotguns completely wrong.
"The most persistent [mistake] that you still occasionally see is shotguns being completely less than lethal, or non-lethal, even, at a set distance," Ferguson tells me, although he does note that “I think a lot of developers have wised up on this.”
"The more and more detail we see incorporated in games, the more they're able to make it resemble reality a bit more,” Ferguson tells me.
There are few people better-equipped to answer a developer’s questions about firearms than Ferguson, who not only reacts to in-game guns for the EXP YouTube channel but is also a gamer himself. His understanding of the needs of gameplay over raw historical accuracy made him an ideal fit for consulting on Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, although developer Expression Games’ realistic depiction of shotguns with authentic (even slightly generous) range is less to do with his consultancy than the studio doing its homework across the era’s entire arsenal.
“I didn't need to tell them that the K50M submachine gun existed and was specific to the North Vietnamese,” explains Ferguson. “They already knew that. So they'd done their due diligence there."
Beyond the shotgun issue, Ferguson often finds himself picking up on minutiae. "There are lots of little tiny details, like realistic patterns of cartridge case ejection for example,” he tells me, “which really don't matter to how the game is played, but if you notice them, adds to it.”
Through his appearances on Firearms Expert Reacts videos, Ferguson has built a reputation for picking apart the details many players won’t even notice. And so in the matter of case ejection patterns, he recognises there’s a bigger picture.
Pistol slides don't move like games think they do.
It's certainly true that the years of shotguns effectively being little more than loud knives is drawing to a close, across not only mil-sims but blockbusters, too. Both Insurgency: Sandstorm and Red Dead Redemption 2 are notable for their more realistic depictions of shotguns.

ビーズ株式会社の趣味グッズブランドBIBILABは10月15日、猫飼いゲーマー専用ウェア「 にゃんガルーパーカー3 」を発売した。MとLの2サイズで展開され、AmazonのBIBILABストアでの価格は8900円（税込）。
本製品は、お腹部分の大きなポケットが特徴のルームウェア「にゃんガルーパーカー」シリーズの最新作だ。そのポケットに愛猫をすっぽり収納し、“ネコハラ”を受けながらも、両手フリーでゲームなどに没頭できる。
「にゃんガルーパーカー3」には、横40×縦23×マチ8cmの大きなボックス型ポケットがお腹部分に配置。そこに愛猫に入ってもらうことで、まるでカンガルーの親子のように一緒に過ごすことができる。愛猫になるべく長く滞在してもらえるように、居心地の良さを追求して設計され、また大型種やぽっちゃり猫にも対応しているとのこと。
